title: console: a user with no personal locale gets the browser's language, never the app's declared `i18n.defaultLocale` (served as discovery `locale.default`)
body:
Found by a downstream app on the published 18.4.0 packages (steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#67, PR #72: the app's default moved to `zh-CN`).

## Symptom

App `i18n.defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`; `GET /api/v1/discovery` answers `locale.default: 'zh-CN'`; the server notifies a no-locale user in Chinese. But the **console** for a user whose `sys_user.locale` is null, in an `en-US` browser, renders English (`Accounts` / `New`, `<html lang="en-US">`). With a `zh-CN` browser it renders Chinese; with `sys_user.locale = 'en'` it renders English regardless (correct).

## Producer (downstream reading)

`@objectstack/console` 18.4.0 i18n runtime resolves the UI language as `sys_user.locale` → `navigator.language` → `'en'`; it never reads the discovery `locale.default`. So the declared app default reaches the server's texts but not the UI — two faces of one setting disagree.

## Suggested fix shape (for the lane to judge)

Resolve the console language as `sys_user.locale` → the app's declared default (discovery `locale.default`) → browser → `en`, or make the precedence of the browser vs the app default an explicit, documented setting; either way the console and the server should answer the same language for the same user.

Dedupe words: console default language · defaultLocale ignored · navigator.language · discovery locale.default · no personal locale.
